text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- Cruising companies worldwide have chosen Copenhagen and its harbour from among 100 cruise destinations as the best port of call in Europe and number three in the world, behind St. Thomas and Barbados.

--- An agreement between the government, liberals and conservatives to avoid an investigation of Denmark's nuclear policy after 1968 is crumbling away as a number of social democratic MPs led by environment minister Svend Auken want to clarify Danish nuclear policy under conservative/liberal rule in the 80s.

--- Danish travel agencies' boycott of SAS after its decision on halving agencies' commissions for selling SAS tickets has come to an end with a new agreement between the two parties, but customers may have to pay more for SAS tickets in future.
--- Danish companies hire new managers too quickly, not checking backgrounds carefully and attaching more importance to formal education and appearance, a new survey shows.
--- Industrial companies with exports to the US and companies competing with US companies benefit from the stong US dollar, which rose to 6.25 crowns on Wednesday.
--- A shortage of titanium for spare parts is forcing SAS to keep more aircraft on the ground. The reason is that golf club manufacturers have bought up most of the titanium market.
